::: {#sol-dropout-scale}

So that each [unit](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-unit)'s expected value during training equals its value at prediction time.
A [unit](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-unit) with value $h$ becomes 0 with probability $p$,
and $h / (1 - p)$ with probability $1 - p$,
so its expected value is

$$
p \cdot 0 + (1 - p) \cdot \frac{h}{1 - p} = h.
$$

The next layer then sees inputs of the same size on average in both modes.

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
_ = torch.manual_seed(0)
_ = dropout.train()
mean_kept = dropout(torch.ones(100_000)).mean().item()
print(mean_kept)
```

Averaged over 100,000 ones,
`nn.Dropout(p=0.5)` in training mode gives `r sprintf("%.3f", py$mean_kept)`.

:::
